core_obligations: The family (proof lines 1066-1072): a set of abelian sheaves is chosen so that every subsheaf of every standard object maps into one of them, which makes the family large enough to test injectivity.

The candidate (proof lines 1072-1082): the product of the chosen sheaves is taken as the candidate injective sheaf and the map into it is defined by the chosen maps out of the subsheaves of the standard objects.

Conclusion (proof lines 1082-1087): the criterion for injectivity of a sheaf shows that the candidate is injective, since test morphisms extend by construction, and the assignment is functorial, so the category has functorial injective embeddings and hence enough injectives.
proof_roadmap: Choose a family of sheaves meeting every subsheaf of every standard object.
Take the product of the family and map into it using the chosen maps.
Verify the injectivity criterion and note functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that the category of abelian sheaves on a site has enough injectives and in fact a functorial injective embedding (statement lines 1058-1064). The proof is a complete construction: a family of sheaves meeting every subsheaf of every standard object is chosen (proof lines 1066-1072), the product of the family is taken as the candidate injective sheaf with the map into it built from the chosen maps (proof lines 1072-1082), and the injectivity criterion for sheaves shows that the candidate is injective while the construction is functorial (proof lines 1082-1087). The non-formal content is the choice of the family and the verification through the criterion. The claim is H2.
